subject: MAP: Helios pilot benchmarking scope & acceptance matrix
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Helios pilot benchmarking scope & acceptance matrix

Hi Emma —

As discussed in our kickoff, attached is a first-pass MAP benchmarking workbook (helios-map-workbook-v1.xlsx) and a proposal for the acceptance matrix. Goal of this thread: lock the performance scope so we can schedule the runs in staging next week and align the MAP close timeline.

High-level proposed approach:
- Workload slices: conversational (short prompt, 128 tokens), long form (500+ tokens), embedding batch (up to 2048 vectors)
- Test types: cold-start single-request latency, steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), concurrency sweep (1–250 concurrent users), TTFT (time-to-first-token) under 95th percentile traffic patterns
- Environments: HLX-staging (profiled), HLX-prod-replay (sanitized traces)
- Measurement: token-level traces + Redwood runtime metrics (batching, KV cache hit rate)

Suggested SLOs / acceptance criteria (draft):
- TTFT: median < 120ms, p95 < 400ms
- Latency (generation): median < 250ms per request, p99 < 1.2s
- Throughput: sustained 8k tokens/sec cluster-level for conversational slice; per-GPU baseline documented in workbook
- Concurrency: maintain latency SLOs at 200 concurrent sessions for conversational; graceful degradation beyond 250

Pass/fail matrix (summary):
- Green: all three priority slices meet SLOs across two runs (separated by 24h)

From: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@heliosanalytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@heliosanalytics.com
Date: 2026-03-01T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Helios pilot benchmarking scope & acceptance matrix

Thanks Logan — this looks thorough. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data & traffic profile: we can provide a sanitized production trace for the conversational slice (peak qps ~520 across geo) and a smaller long-form set (10k examples).
2) Concurrency expectations: our peak concurrent sessions are close to 180 globally; we prefer tests that show behavior up to 300 to validate headroom.
3) Security: SOC 2 controls are required for any staging data; we'll only share sanitized traces.

We reviewed the draft SLOs and would like p95 TTFT to be <= 350ms (we can be flexible on median). Also want an explicit degradation policy — e.g., if p99 latency exceeds 2x SLO, auto-fallback to smaller model variant.

I'll upload the traces to the Drive link once they are scrubbed. Tentatively good to run in staging on 2026-03-02 / 03.

— Emma
Senior Infrastructure Lead
Helios Analytics

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Helios pilot benchmarking scope & acceptance matrix

Emma — thanks, that aligns well. Updated plan and acceptance matrix attached (acceptance-matrix-v0.2.pdf) and I pushed a small workbook update with per-GPU throughput baselines. Key updates per your ask:

- TTFT p95 relaxed to 350ms for the MAP (we keep median targets tighter)
- Degradation policy: automatic model variant fallback + circuit-breaker if p99 > 2x p99-SLO for 5 consecutive minutes; this will be included in the runbook
- Concurrency sweep: we'll run incremental sweeps at 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300 concurrent sessions; collect KV cache hit rates and continuous-batching stats

Run schedule proposal (finalize by tomorrow):
- 2026-03-02 09:00 UTC: preparatory baseline run (single node)
- 2026-03-03 03:00 UTC & 15:00 UTC: two full-sweep runs (multi-node)

Success criteria for MAP close (commercial gating):
- Three priority slices green across at least one multi-node run AND no unresolved regressions against production traces
- Performance regression alerting hooks verified in Console
- CS & Security sign-off on sanitized trace usage

Action items:
- Emma: upload sanitized traces and confirm 2026-03-02 run window (ETA: EOD 2026-03-01)
- Marissa: confirm commercial milestones for conditional close if runs pass
- Aditya: prep run templates and add fallback policy config to the staging cluster

[Attachment: helios-map-workbook-v1.xlsx]

— Logan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick update — we completed the first multi-node sweep this morning. Preliminary: conversational slice met median & p95 TTFT and median latency targets; p99 for long-form exceeded our p99 threshold in one run (investigating).

We uploaded raw results: hlx-staging-results-20260303.csv and a notes doc in Drive. Next steps per our side:
- We will let you know within 24 hours if the long-form p99 is a data artifact (we suspect a single outlier sample).
- If confirmed, assume green and proceed with the conditional PO flow.

Thanks for the clear runbook — made the execution fast.
